skills_considered.reason: The discovery ledger is a research surface owned by other batches; every transferable lesson here is proposed as a commit candidate instead of written into the ledger.
A gene-replacement lesson from another gene is not a WWOX therapeutic hypothesis; forging one would convert a stated transfer limit into a lead.
No small molecule with a SMILES is proposed, so the BLOCK-1 ADMET gate has nothing to triage.
Scientists do not touch the four current files; every change is proposed as a commit candidate.
The triples are published for a blind auditor; a reader cannot audit their own locators.

entries.proposition: The adult arm received four times the vector of the neonatal arm, so age and antigen load are not matched.
entries.snippet: the doses administered to adult mice were four times higher than to neonatal mice

entries.proposition: No transgene protein survived in the adult brain, by either route, and the loss came with neuronal loss.
entries.snippet: The elevation of glial and immune markers was coupled with reduced neuronal density and undetectable Cas9 protein expression

entries.proposition: The absence of the protein did not depend on which adult route was used.
entries.snippet: The absence of detectable Cas9 protein occurred irrespective of whether the adult injections were made via the i.c.v. or i.c. routes of administration
resulted in a significant reduction of neuronal density compared with the three control treatment groups

entries.proposition: Neonatal delivery kept the transgene and provoked no adaptive cellular response.
entries.snippet: Cas9 expression is maintained and does not trigger neuroinflammatory responses even after full maturation

entries.proposition: Early expression did not prevent an antibody response at either age.
entries.snippet: neither treatment time point circumvented eliciting a humoral immune response

entries.proposition: Neonatal priming reduced but did not abolish the harm of a later dose.
entries.snippet: lowers, but does not entirely eliminate, the neurotoxic and inflammatory effects of administering this construct to the adult CNS

entries.proposition: A different foreign protein in the same compartment at the same age caused neither toxicity nor inflammation.
entries.snippet: indicating that EGFP did not elicit neurotoxic or neuroinflammatory responses

entries.proposition: A neuron-restricted promoter may itself impede tolerance induction.
entries.snippet: the use of the SynI promoter may have hampered the development of Cas9-reactive T

entries.proposition: The capsid and genome alone were weak immune activators by this route.
entries.snippet: the AAV9 vector itself was not a potent activator of immunity 1 month post-injection

entries.proposition: Cytokine transcripts did not rise in any group despite the histological activation.
entries.snippet: changes in cytokine expression levels were too low to be detected
